analysis.title: Americas Capital Markets: LPLA and SF October Monthly Metrics
key_insights: LPLA October NNA was $7.0bn, a 3.3% annualized organic growth rate, in line with the ~3% messaged at earnings. The weakness came from one large attrition item that reversed the large win in August.
LPLA client cash balances were $55.9bn versus $56.6bn in September. Quarterly fee billings were a $2.6bn headwind to cash, so cash growth excluding fee billings was +$1.9bn (+3% m/m).
LPLA client assets ended October at $2.561tn, flat m/m and +9% y/y. Advisory generated ~$8.2bn of net new assets and brokerage had ~$1.2bn of net outflows.
LPLA client cash was 2.2% of client assets. Excluding money market, core client cash was $55.0bn, down 1% m/m. ICA was $37.3bn, DCA $15.6bn, money market sweep $0.9bn and CCA $2.1bn.
LPLA net buying activity was $12.6bn in October.

SF total client assets were $578.9bn, up 0.4% m/m (+$2.4bn) and +5.3% y/y. GS estimates firmwide NNA was flattish, about -$0.5bn, an implied annualized organic growth rate of -1.0% versus -4.7% in September.

SF fee-based client assets rose to $240.8bn (+$1.2bn m/m), with implied annualized organic growth of -0.2% versus -1% in September. PCG fee-based assets rose 1.0% m/m to $211.8bn (+8.8% y/y), with about $1.0bn of estimated net inflows (5.9% annualized).

SF client cash (cash sweep + Smart Rate) fell 1.3% m/m to $23.2bn (-8.9% y/y), or 4.01% of client assets versus 4.08% in September. Treasury deposits rose 4.2% m/m to $13.2bn, so client cash plus Treasury deposits was $36.4bn (+0.6% m/m, +42.8% y/y).
SF net loans grew 1.2% m/m to $26.4bn (+21.0% y/y).

market_movers.rationale: Buy rating and $400 12-month target on ~13x Q5-Q8 P/E. October NNA was weaker as messaged at earnings, and cash trends were better excluding seasonality.
Neutral rating and $76 12-month target on 11x Q5-Q8 P/E, unchanged. October NNA was flattish.

risk_factors: LPLA downside risks: lower interest rates, softer organic growth, slower client cash balance growth, and weaker equity markets.
SF upside risk: higher markets. SF downside risks: weaker markets and slower organic growth.
